problem: Multimodal language models fail to ensure visual evidence supports their answers, allowing models to generate correct answers without grounding them in correct visual regions.
approach: Integrates positive, counterfactual, and random-masking training paradigms with a language-guided pipeline to automatically localize question-relevant regions and generate counterfactual variants, trained with GRPO-based reinforcement learning using three complementary rewards.
contribution: DeFacto substantially improves both answer accuracy and evidence-answer consistency over strong baselines on diverse benchmarks, with new DeFacto-1.5K benchmark for evaluating evidence-grounded consistency.

problem: Large language models' effectiveness in real-world blue team threat-hunting scenarios remains insufficiently explored, as cyber threats grow in scale and sophistication.
approach: CYBERTEAM constructs a standardized workflow in two stages by modeling realistic threat-hunting workflows with task dependencies and addressing each task through operational modules tailored to specific analytical requirements.
contribution: CYBERTEAM integrates 30 tasks and 9 operational modules to guide LLMs through standardized threat analysis, revealing improvements from standardized design while exposing limitations of open-ended reasoning in real-world threat hunting.

problem: Federated adversarial learning enhances robustness but existing work focuses on convergence with limited understanding of generalization capabilities under adversarial perturbations.
approach: Analyzes federated adversarial learning through algorithmic stability, deriving perturbation-dependent generalization bounds via stochastic gradient descent and proposing Moreau envelope optimization for perturbation-independent bounds.
contribution: Establishes unified theoretical framework showing stronger adversarial attacks degrade generalization, with Moreau envelope approach demonstrating efficacy in simultaneously enhancing both robustness and generalization.

problem: Zero-shot 3D scene understanding via 2D vision-language models struggles with retaining task-relevant 3D details under limited input budget and suffers from redundancy among patches across views.
approach: KeyVT uses hierarchical view-to-token transportation with optimal transport framework to select task-relevant views based on semantic content and geometric position, then identifies representative tokens to minimize redundancy.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements over existing tuning-free methods and performance comparable to training-based approaches on three widely used benchmarks for 3D question answering.

problem: Tree-search decoding for language models suffers under fixed per-query token budgets where existing policies are budget-agnostic and risk late-stage over-branching or premature termination.
approach: Budget-Guided MCTS aligns tree-search policy with remaining token budget by starting with broad exploration, then prioritizing refinement and answer completion as budget decreases while reducing late-stage branching.
contribution: Consistently outperforms budget-agnostic tree-search baselines across inference budgets on mathematical reasoning and physics reasoning benchmarks with open-weight LLMs.

problem: Neural networks typically use uniform learning rates across layers despite empirical evidence that layer-specific learning rates accelerate training, but principled understanding of when and why remains limited.
approach: Investigates non-uniform learning rates via Stackelberg optimization, showing smaller learning rates for body layers and larger for final layers can be interpreted as two-time-scale alternating gradient descent on a Stackelberg reformulation.
contribution: Establishes finite-time convergence guarantees and identifies two mechanisms by which non-uniform learning rates outperform uniform ones: Stackelberg objective optimization structure and sharper local curvature.

problem: Determining whether language models have been trained on specific target texts is crucial for privacy and data contamination detection, but existing local token-based methods neglect probability dynamics during generation.
approach: Shifts detection paradigm from local tokens to global sequence perspective using Adaptive Entropic Convolutional Analysis to conceptualize probability sequences as dynamic signals with calibration and convolutional filtering.
contribution: AECA surpasses previous methods by up to 1.5% in average AUC on WikiMIA benchmark with advantages particularly pronounced in long-text scenarios.

problem: Prover-verifier games offer verifiability in classification but have not been applied to complex high-dimensional inputs like images, while concept encodings effectively translate data to interpretable concepts but work with low-capacity predictors.
approach: Neural Concept Verifier combines prover-verifier games for formal verifiability with concept encodings to handle high-dimensional inputs interpretably, using minimally supervised concept discovery to extract structured encodings.
contribution: Outperforms classic concept-based models and pixel-based PVG baselines on high-dimensional logically complex datasets while helping mitigate shortcut behavior.

problem: Standard actor-critic methods like PPO rely on scalar value functions that only estimate expectation of cumulative returns, discarding higher-order statistics and leading to inaccurate value estimation for complex reasoning tasks.
approach: DisPPO integrates non-parametric quantile regression into PPO to model full return distribution, with Wasserstein-metric contraction guarantee for convergence and on-policy framework avoiding off-policy replay instability.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standard PPO and recent baselines on Llama and Qwen models across mathematical reasoning and Text-to-SQL generation in both Pass@1 and Pass@k metrics.

problem: Extracting causally meaningful features from time-series data is challenging when operating conditions change, as existing methods capture either temporal causal relationships or cross-environment invariance but not both simultaneously.
approach: Causal Feature Learning formulates feature extraction as generalized Rayleigh-quotient problem, maximizing correlation with target variables while penalizing sensitivity to environment-dependent mean shifts.
contribution: Achieves 93.69% average fault detection rate on Tennessee Eastman Process, outperforming 15 baseline methods and validating benefit of jointly capturing temporal relevance and environment mean invariance.

problem: Reparameterization policy gradient achieves high sample efficiency but suffers from under-utilization of computationally expensive dynamics Jacobians and inherent training instability under sample reuse.
approach: Reparameterization Proximal Policy Optimization enables sample reuse by showing RPG naturally optimizes PPO-style surrogate objective via backpropagation through time, with clipped policy gradient mechanism and KL divergence regularization.
contribution: Maintains superior sample efficiency and consistently outperforms or achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks while addressing stability concerns.

problem: Large language models can be controlled via prompts and activation steering but existing accounts treat these disparate methodologies separately despite their common goal of controlling behavior.
approach: Develops unifying Bayesian perspective where steering alters concept priors and in-context learning leads to evidence accumulation, producing closed-form model predictive of LLM behavior across interventions.
contribution: Explains empirical phenomena like sigmoidal learning curves and predicts novel ones including additivity in log-belief space and distinct behavioral shift phases from intervention control changes.

problem: Federated learning faces model heterogeneity where architectural differences yield incompatible representations, making knowledge-sharing challenging as proxy models incur high costs and prototype-based carriers cause semantic confusion.
approach: Rule-based federated learning shares interpretable class-discriminative rules via a rule network that unifies clients' decision features, with selective activation of rules relevant to local classes.
contribution: Achieves better accuracy-communication trade-off across heterogeneous settings compared to proxy-model and prototype-based approaches while maintaining personalization.

problem: Handling large-scale incomplete multi-view data poses challenges as anchor-based strategies rely on shallow bipartite graphs failing to capture complex high-order correlations, and treat observed and missing instances indiscriminately.
approach: Hypergraph-Augmented Incomplete Multi-View Clustering constructs consensus anchor-guided hypergraph modeling group-wise interactions with dual-adaptive reweighting mechanism calibrating importance at view and sample levels.
contribution: Achieves superior clustering accuracy and maintains high efficiency even in scenarios with severe data incompleteness, validated across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Large language models are prone to hallucination and untruthful responses particularly when tasks demand information outside their parametric knowledge, as approaches optimizing accuracy often amplify hallucinations.
approach: TruthRL implements GRPO with ternary reward distinguishing correct answers, hallucinations, and abstentions to incentivize models reducing hallucinations through both correct responses and abstention when uncertain.
contribution: Significantly reduces hallucinations (43.5% to 19.4% on benchmarks) and improves truthfulness (5.3% to 37.2%) across four knowledge-intensive benchmarks with gains across various backbone models.

problem: Multi-task learning with shared linear representations remains underdeveloped for likelihood-based efficiently solvable algorithms due to non-convex structure intrinsic to matrix factorization.
approach: Proposes first-order algorithm jointly learning shared representation and task-specific parameters with guaranteed efficiency, achieving convergence in Õ(1) iterations via likelihood-based optimization.
contribution: Attains near-optimal estimation error of Õ(dk/(TN)), improving over existing likelihood-based methods by a factor of k where d, k, T, N denote input dimension, representation dimension, task count, and samples per task.

problem: Test-time scaling methods like majority voting depend critically on error distribution across samples as concentrated errors degrade aggregation and suppress exploration in iterative refinement.
approach: D-FUSEr introduces theoretically grounded diverse failure reward incentivizing calibrated disagreement in model errors, with anti-votes predicting common mistakes to explicitly reweight probability mass.
contribution: Substantially improves majority vote and iterative refinement performance across three model families and four benchmarks without degrading single-sample accuracy.

problem: Large language models struggle with structural understanding when processing graph topologies in serialized format despite demonstrating remarkable semantic understanding.
approach: SLASH analyzes internal LLM attention mechanisms finding spontaneous graph topology reconstruction via sawtooth patterns in attention maps, then proposes attention redistribution to amplify structural understanding.
contribution: Delivers significant and consistent performance gains across diverse LLMs on graph tasks and molecular prediction with training-free solution requiring only attention redistribution.

problem: Training large-scale generative models is resource-intensive and relies on heuristic dataset weighting while it remains unclear if experts can be combined modularly to match monolithic performance robustly.
approach: Formulates modular generative modeling as minimax game to find robust gate minimizing divergence to worst-case data mixture, proven to exist via Kakutani's fixed-point theorem with modularity as strong regularizer.
contribution: Proves modular approach theoretically outperforms models retrained on aggregate data with gap characterized by Jensen-Shannon divergence, with scalable Stochastic Primal-Dual algorithm and Structural Distillation.

problem: Multi-agent systems using large language models introduce trustworthiness concerns as adversarial agents can inject misleading information that propagates contagiously, corrupting benign agents.
approach: Models multi-agent communication as signed directed acyclic graph computing each agent's contribution to final decision via backward propagation for accurate identification and isolation of malicious agents.
contribution: Notably outperforms existing multi-agent system defense mechanisms in complex and dynamic environments, providing effective guardrail for trustworthy multi-agent system deployment.

problem: Machine learning attacks on Learning with Errors with binary or small secrets succeed only on simple settings and fail to recover denser secrets or larger Hamming weights.
approach: Shows larger training sets and repeated examples allow recovery of denser secrets with observed power-law relationship, introducing stepwise regression technique to recover cool bits of the secret.
contribution: Allows recovery of denser binary secrets up to Hamming weight 70 for dimension 256 and 75 for dimension 512 (versus 33 and 63 in previous works), with substantial improvements on denser ternary secrets.

problem: Equivariant neural networks for general linear symmetries remain limited as most are built for compact groups, restricting reuse on matrix-valued data like covariances or shape tensors.
approach: Introduces Reductive Lie Neurons that achieve exact GL(n)-equivariance natively supporting matrix-valued and Lie-algebraic features using non-degenerate adjoint-invariant bilinear form.
contribution: Matches or outperforms strong equivariant and self-supervised baselines while using substantially fewer parameters and compute, with consistent improvements across diverse symmetry groups.

problem: Multimodal language models face security threats from visual prompt injection attacks with existing defenses lacking principled understanding of mechanisms and struggling to balance efficiency and fidelity.
approach: Localizes critical image tokens via gradient analysis then neutralizes through masking, introducing Hidden-State Gradient Norm score for adversarial behavior attribution with theoretical consistency guarantees.
contribution: Reduces attack success rates to near zero while preserving model utility with negligible computational overhead, requiring only single forward-backward pass to identify and mask tokens.

problem: Machine learning weather forecasting models suffer from spectral degradation from training to predict ensemble mean deterministically and compressive encoding creating information bottlenecks.
approach: MOSAIC combines learned functional perturbations for ensemble forecasting with block-sparse attention sharing keys and values across spatially adjacent queries to capture long-range dependencies at linear cost.
contribution: At 1.5° resolution matches or outperforms models trained on 0.25° data on IFS HRES with individual ensemble members exhibiting near-perfect spectral alignment across all resolved frequencies.

problem: Self-interpretation methods prompting language models to describe internal states remain unreliable due to hyperparameter sensitivity in LLMs.
approach: Trains lightweight adapters on interpretability artifacts while keeping LM frozen, using scalar affine adapter with only d_model+1 parameters to generate feature labels from sparse autoencoders.
contribution: Generates sparse autoencoder feature labels outperforming training labels (70% versus 50% at 70B), identifies topics with 94% recall@1, decodes bridge entities in reasoning without chain-of-thought.

problem: Learning optimal individualized dosing policies to maximize utility faces high experimental costs imposing strict budget constraints, with continuous dosing and policy optimization underexplored in active learning.
approach: Active learning framework exploiting dose-response curve structure showing policy optimization regret bounded by expected posterior gradient variance, with batch acquisition strategy minimizing target gradient variance.
contribution: GVALID achieves superior performance under strict budget constraints on optimal policy learning for individualized dosing.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation systems remain brittle under realistic retrieval noise as retrievers and rerankers optimize for relevance alone, selecting trivial or unsuitable evidence for generators.
approach: BAR-RAG reframes reranker as boundary-aware evidence selector targeting generator's Goldilocks Zone through reinforcement learning using generator feedback and two-stage fine-tuning pipeline.
contribution: Consistently improves end-to-end performance under noisy retrieval achieving average gain of 10.3% over strong RAG and reranking baselines while substantially improving robustness.

problem: Online learning for Cox proportional hazards model is challenging because partial likelihood is non-decomposable with each risk set requiring summation over all samples.
approach: COLSA replaces partial likelihood with full likelihood using sieve approximation of baseline hazard, maintaining sufficient statistics for higher-order basis with data-driven basis projection.
contribution: Achieves asymptotic normality and statistical efficiency matching pooled-data partial likelihood estimator without accessing full data and only requiring constant memory.

problem: Continual learning on long task sequences struggles to effectively learn discriminative and comprehensive feature representations while maintaining stability and plasticity across 100+ tasks.
approach: CaRE uses bi-level routing mixture-of-experts with router selection stage dynamically activating task-specific routers and expert routing phase for dynamic expert aggregation across network layers.
contribution: First continual learner scaling to 100-300+ non-overlapping tasks significantly outperforming all baselines, with new OmniBenchmark-1K dataset for very long task sequences.

problem: Users accessing large language models via black-box APIs must transmit sensitive prompts, outputs, and fine-tuning data to external providers, creating critical privacy risks at API boundary.
approach: AlienLM provides API-only privacy layer translating text into Alien Language via vocabulary-scale bijection enabling lossless recovery, with Alien Adaptation Training adapting models to operate on alienized inputs.
contribution: Retains over 81% of plaintext-oracle performance on average substantially outperforming baselines, recovering fewer than 0.22% of alienized tokens under adversaries with model weights access.

problem: Generating long-horizon molecular dynamics is difficult due to error accumulation in time-domain autoregressive models causing drift and fixed step-size constraints on temporal resolution.
approach: BioDynaSpec reformulates protein dynamics as spatio-spectral generation via Independent Windowed Fourier Decomposition combined with low-to-high frequency autoregression and diffusion denoising.
contribution: Improves 250-frame trajectory generation with R_250=1.509 Å reducing error by 60.4% versus MDGEN and 57.2% versus ProAR, achieving best PCA and distribution matching metrics.

problem: Computational protein design requires substantial domain expertise with traditional physics-based methods or relies on restricted functional ontologies that fail to bridge semantic gap between text and protein sequences.
approach: PDAgent uses LLM-driven autonomous agent framework with ReAct reasoning loop implementing five phases (think, plan, act, observe, reflect) integrating template retrieval and conservation-aware mutation.
contribution: Achieves 91.86% average constraint satisfaction rate with high structural quality (mean pLDDT 87.69) substantially outperforming direct LLM generation and specialized deep learning methods.

problem: Semi-supervised learning faces challenges in realistic scenarios where labeled data is scarce and unlabeled data follows unknown arbitrary distributions with pseudo-labeling methods prone to erroneous labels.
approach: SAGE leverages inter-sample relations for structural inference using simplex anchored graph-state equipartition capturing high-order dependencies, with simplex equiangular tight frame guiding representation separation.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on five standard benchmarks with average accuracy gain of 8.52% by bypassing distribution estimation via structural consensus.

problem: High-fidelity solubility prediction must couple molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior across diverse chemical environments but existing methods sacrifice interpretability for predictive power.
approach: DISSOLVR challenges this trend by developing transparent framework using physically-grounded descriptors with LLM-assisted post-hoc explanation pipeline bridging symbolic artifacts and chemically grounded narratives.
contribution: Approaches aleatoric limit of experimental uncertainty achieving out-of-distribution generalization through structural invariance without requiring non-transparent architectures.

problem: Graph convolutional networks treat adjacent nodes as equally important and may limit representational power by failing to capture highly correlated information between nonadjacent nodes.
approach: Global Interacted Graph Convolutional Network leverages Dominant Set solution vectors to adaptively characterize global importance distribution over all nodes modulating message passing across layers.
contribution: Effectively captures highly correlated information between nonadjacent nodes emphasizing critical graph-level information while enhancing discriminative power with optimized memory complexity.

problem: Heterogeneous federated learning approaches often rely on sharing model parameters or representations exposing sensitive information and incurring overhead.
approach: SoHip enables collaboration via memory sharing rather than model sharing, abstracting agents' short-term memory into individual long-term memory through hippocampus-inspired mechanism.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods achieving up to 8.78% accuracy improvements while preserving on-device raw data and local models with only lightweight memory exchange.

problem: Machine learning interatomic potentials follow scaling laws but lack scalable distributed training systems due to double-backward execution pattern creating mismatch with existing systems.
approach: JanusPipe integrates SymFold for memory-efficient pipeline parallelism with WaveK reducing pipeline bubbles by balancing four-phase compute time in 3D-parallel training.
contribution: Improves throughput by 1.51× and 1.45× on average over 1F1B and Hanayo respectively on 32 GPUs for machine learning interatomic potential training.

problem: Understanding what generative models retain from training data remains challenging beyond verbatim reproduction with subtle traces exploitable for membership inference.
approach: Analyzes Rectified Flows interpolation path finding gap between train and test data reconstruction following bell-shaped curve over interpolation parameter that accumulates during training.
contribution: Shows bell-shaped membership signal structure is universal with peak location derivable in closed form under Gaussian assumptions, enabling membership inference attack exploiting λ-resolved structure.

problem: Visual document retrieval models are historically repurposed from generative VLMs but this design choice constrains performance in multi-vector embedding settings.
approach: ModernVBERT systematically develops VDR models from ground up through controlled experiments isolating key training factors including attention masking and contrastive objectives.
contribution: Trains 250M-parameter vision-language encoder outperforming recent models up to 10 times its size on document retrieval tasks while enabling efficient CPU inference.

problem: Goal-conditioned policies' downstream performance is highly sensitive to discrete text prompts but bypassing text limitations through latent control remains underexplored.
approach: Preference Goal Tuning formulates post-training as latent control where goal embedding serves as continuous control variable to modulate frozen policy behavior optimized with trajectory-level preference objective.
contribution: Achieves average relative improvements of 72.0% and 81.6% on Minecraft tasks with minimal data, surpassing full fine-tuning by 13.4% in out-of-distribution settings.
